payload.title: HTTP
payload.summary: Implement a bounded HTTP/1.1 message subset with borrowed spans, strict framing, and deadline-based stream I/O.

prerequisites: POSIX sockets and TCP byte streams
Protocol errors, system-call errors, and bounded buffers
outcomes: Construct a small HTTP/1.1 request without allocation
Parse requests and responses into non-owning spans
Separate HTTP message framing from TCP reads
Reject ambiguous framing and recognize premature EOF

events.label: Share one deadline
events.detail: send_message, recv_message, and serve_one preserve partial progress without refreshing the operation timeout.

events.label: Fragment POST /demo
events.detail: The client sends POST /demo with Content-Length: 4 and body ping in two-byte chunks.

events.label: Find header terminator
events.detail: Parsing waits for the CRLF CRLF boundary inside the header limit before trusting Content-Length.

events.label: Read Content-Length body
events.detail: The four declared request body bytes must all arrive before the request view is complete.

events.label: Send fixed 200 response
events.detail: serve_one replies with HTTP/1.1 200 OK, Content-Length: 2, and body OK.

events.label: Fragment response bytes
events.detail: A separate receive fixture fragments a 200 response in three-byte writes while declaring Content-Length: 5.

events.label: Assemble hello body
events.detail: recv_message succeeds only after all five Content-Length bytes for hello are present.

events.label: Reject premature EOF
events.detail: A response declaring Content-Length: 4 but delivering only ab before close returns TRUNCATED.

events.label: Reject chunked coding
events.detail: Transfer-Encoding: chunked is MALFORMED because chunked framing is a non-goal.

events.label: Keep TLS out of scope
events.detail: TLS is not modeled; this lesson stays on plaintext bounded localhost streams.

payload.exercise: Implement deterministic request construction, strict Content-Length parsing, shared-deadline socket loops, and the fixed-response serve_one path in exercise.c.
payload.reference: Use solution.c only after preserving every initialized-output, limit, and framing rule in lesson.h.
checks: Exact request bytes and borrowed request/response views
Invalid arguments, small buffers, truncated bodies, and bounded limits
Rejection of transfer encoding, obsolete folding, and conflicting or invalid lengths
Fragmented localhost send/receive under one monotonic deadline
serve_one propagation of truncation, timeout, malformed input, and capacity failures

allowed: Caller-supplied storage and borrowed message views
excluded: External networking, raw capture, or privileged operations
Heap allocation or global mutable state
Production HTTP features such as TLS, chunking, proxies, compression, or pipelining
